subject: Renewal planning: Sales engagement sequence stack — decision and negotiation plan
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning: Sales engagement sequence stack — decision and negotiation plan

Team,

Our Outreach and SalesLoft contracts come up for renewal in mid-August (exact dates attached in Marissa's sheet). I want us to treat this as a single decision: keep both, consolidate to one vendor, or explore a migration+hybrid approach. Key constraints: predictable per-seat spend, minimal disruption to active cadences, and better measurement for SDR/AE workflows.

Quick facts I pulled:
- Current blended spend ~ $410k/yr across Outreach + SalesLoft.
- Active sequence users: ~120 (SDR + AEs + CS teams) with heavy usage in EMEA/US.
- We have a history of custom integrations (2 HubSpot sync apps) and a handful of Zapier-based automations.

Ask: please review and add notes to the attached renewal analysis. Prioritize: 1) total cost of ownership over 12 months, 2) migration complexity, 3) enablement hours required, 4) any license consolidation discounts.

I propose we:
- Get best-and-final offers from Outreach and SalesLoft by next Wednesday (6/23).
- Engage Pax Partners for a fixed-fee migration scoping exercise if we lean to migrate.
- Loop legal (Connor) for standard exceptions and data-processing terms early.

I'll set a 30-minute sync if needed; for now flag major blockers in the sheet.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

[attachment: none yet — awaiting Marissa's analysis]
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning: Sales engagement sequence stack — decision and negotiation plan

Karthik — attaching the workbook with line-item costs and usage metrics. High-level takeaways below and comments in the sheet.

Attachments: Sales_Engagement_Renewal_Analysis.xlsx (Excel, 48 KB)

Summary:
- Outreach (current primary for SDRs): list price ~ $270k/yr; current net ~ $240k/yr after historical discounts.
- SalesLoft: list price ~ $210k/yr; current net ~ $200k/yr.
- Combined churn/overlap inefficiency estimated at ~$35k/yr (duplicate seats, redundant sequences).
- Enablement costs to move ~ 4–6 weeks of internal SE time + vendor enablement. Pax Partners estimate (rough) $28k–$40k for migration scope.

Risks & negotiation levers:
- Consolidating to a single vendor will reduce licensing overhead but will require at least one migration sprint and re-validation of HubSpot syncs.
- We can push for: multi-year commitment discount, migration credits, waived onboarding fees, and pilot credits for new features (analytics, intent scoring).

Recommendation (tentative): ask Outreach for best-and-final including a migration credit and an enterprise enablement package. Outreach currently supports a couple of features we rely on (sequence-level A/B testing) and their reported tokenization of cadences matches our usage. But ask SalesLoft to match with an enablement credit and a fixed-cost migration package from Pax.

I'll join vendor calls and walk through the workbook line by line; Connor, please flag any T&Cs we must standardize early (data retention, API rate limits).

Marissa
Sales Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Alicia Park <alicia.park@outreach.io>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Outreach renewal options & migration credit proposal for Redwood Inference

Hi Karthik — great to reconnect after last quarter's usage review. I pulled options for your renewal window (Aug 2026).

Attached: Outreach_Renewal_Quote.pdf (PDF, 124 KB)

Proposal highlights:
- 10% renewal discount on current net ARR with a 2-year committment.
- One-time migration credit: $25,000 toward professional services (can be applied to Pax Partners or our in-house team).
- Included: 40 hours of enablement, sequence audit, and 2 custom HubSpot sync reviews.
- Optional add-on: Outreach Amplify pilot (30 days, up to 2,000 contacts) for free if signed before 7/10/2026.

We are happy to put the renewal into DocuSign and draft an SOW that restricts rate-limit changes and preserves current API access. If you want, I can also secure a one-off clause for a 30-day rollback window post-migration.

Would you and Marissa be available for a 45-minute call on Thursday 6/24 to walk the quote and ask for a final revision?

Thanks —
Alicia Park
Senior Account Executive, Outreach
alicia.park@outreach.io | (415) 555-0183

[attachment: Outreach_Renewal_Quote.pdf]
From: David Chen <david.chen@salesloft.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 09:37:00 -0700
Subject: SalesLoft counter-proposal & migration support

Karthik / Marissa — thanks for the heads-up. We reviewed your usage and can present a counter that addresses the migration + enablement ask.

Attachments: SalesLoft_Proposal.pdf (PDF, 96 KB)

Counter-offer summary:
- 12% discount on list for a 1-year renewal with option to extend at a pre-agreed price.
- 6 months of complimentary enablement (remote) + 20 hours of Pax Partners at a discounted rate to assist migration.
- Commitment to a shared migration playbook and a dedicated Success Manager for 6 months.

If consolidation is a priority, we can offer an additional rebate for multi-team seat conversion (details in the attachment). Happy to join a vendor call on 6/24 or 6/25.

Best,
David Chen
Enterprise Sales, SalesLoft
david.chen@salesloft.com | (617) 555-0122
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alicia Park <alicia.park@outreach.io>, David Chen <david.chen@salesloft.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 15:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning: Sales engagement sequence stack — decision and negotiation plan

Team / Vendors — quick summary and next steps so we're all aligned.

Summary: we have competing vendor offers on the table. Outreach: 10% + $25k migration credit + 40h enablement. SalesLoft: 12% + 6 months enablement + Pax Partners discounted hours. Marissa's analysis shows Outreach is slightly higher net today but offers a simpler path to preserve existing configurations.

Next steps (action owners):
- Karthik: run a 30-min internal scoring matrix (cost, migration risk, analytics parity) and share by EOD Monday 6/22.
- Marissa: update the workbook with vendor-specific line items from the PDFs and flag integration blockers.
- Connor: please prepare a 1-page exceptions list we cannot accept (data retention, vendor subprocessor list, rollback language) by 6/22 COB.
- Vendors (Alicia / David): please provide a final, best-and-final quote (updated PDF + redlined SOW) by 6/23. We will schedule a 45-min vendor consolidation call on 6/24 11:00 AM PT to move to closure.

Connor — add legal's standard DPAs and highlight any new subprocessor requests.

If you can get the DocuSign stub (Alicia) and SalesLoft final PDF (David) in before 6/23 it will help the decision. We will aim to consolidate to a single vendor unless the cost of migration + enablement materially exceeds the ongoing run-rate benefit.

Thanks all —
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Revenue, Redwood Inference
